mcat_description.short: Temporary Buildings are factory-built, demountable prefabricated structures — including portable site offices, labour camps, storage sheds, and modular rooms — assembled on-site from steel-framed, sandwich-panel components and designed to be relocated or dismantled after use.
mcat_description.long: Temporary Buildings in the Indian B2B market refer to prefabricated modular structures manufactured off-site using cold-formed or hot-rolled steel frames combined with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rock wool core), then transported and assembled on-site without permanent foundations. They serve as construction site offices, labour colonies, security cabins, storage sheds, canteens, and event or emergency shelters across industrial, infrastructure, and institutional projects. Structural steel components are typically IS 2062-certified, and load design follows IS 875 (wind/live loads) and IS 14687 (temporary works). The key commercial differentiator from permanent prefab buildings is their portability, relocatability, and absence of permanent civil works — enabling reuse across multiple project sites.

market_context: In India, 'Temporary Buildings' commercially refers to factory-built, demountable prefabricated structures — primarily portable site office cabins, labour accommodation buildings, and storage sheds — supplied to construction contractors, infrastructure developers, and industrial buyers. The dominant construction system uses cold-formed steel frames with insulated sandwich panels (PUF, EPS, or rock wool core), enabling rapid on-site assembly without permanent foundations. The modular prefabricated segment (portable cabins, guardrooms, semi-permanent buildings) was valued at approximately Rs 17 billion in FY24 and is projected to grow at 10–12% annually to FY29, driven by infrastructure investment and construction activity. Structural steel components follow IS 2062 certification; load design references IS 875 (wind and live loads) and IS 14687 (temporary works falsework); BIS has published IS 15916 and IS 15917 as codes of practice for prefabricated building design and erection. Key Indian manufacturers include EPACK Prefab, Kirby Building Systems, Tata BlueScope Steel, Everest Industries, and SAMAN Portable. The market remains moderately fragmented with a large unorganised sector competing on price. Buyers in this MCAT are predominantly B2B — construction contractors, EPC companies, and industrial facilities managers — with a smaller but growing segment of individual homeowners seeking rooftop/terrace room additions (evidenced by keyword 'temporary room on terrace price'). Quoting is per unit for standard cabin configurations and per sq ft for custom or large-span structures.
